text: Knowledge
An *identity* is a unique cryptographic key pair.
A *party* to a contract is whoever has an identity, and a *person* is a party who established their own identity.
Alice, Bob and Carol are persons.
1. ○ Establish: Alice may establish an identity once. Alice will make herself known by her public key, sign her acts with her private key, and be accountable for every act signed with it.
2. ■ Acquaint: Alice and Bob may jointly come to know each other.
3. ■ Introduce: Alice may introduce Carol to Bob with the consent of Bob, provided Alice and Bob know each other and Alice knows Carol.
Friendship
Friendship inherits from Knowledge.
Alice *trusts* Bob when she knows Bob personally and believes him to keep the undertakings he signs under grassroots contracts.
Alice and Bob are persons.
1. ○ Befriend: Alice and Bob, who trust each other and are not friends, may jointly become friends.
2. ■ Unfriend: Alice may end her friendship with Bob.
3. ○ Loss of Trust. Alice will end her friendship with Bob if she ceases to trust him.
Guardians
Guardians inherits from Friendship.

A *relation* is a friendship or the membership of a group. Bob *trusts* Wendy, a ward of Alice, when he trusts Alice. The *decision rule*, which the creator of a ward decides, says who decides for a ward and how. A ward takes an act of a party by those who decide for the ward.
Alice and Bob are persons, Wendy and Will wards.
1. ■ Enter: Alice may create a ward, Wendy, and establish Wendy's identity by choosing Wendy's key pair. Alice is then the creator, a guardian and a friend of Wendy.

2. ■ Guardian decisions. Make guardian: Those who decide for Wendy may make Bob, a friend of a guardian of Wendy, a guardian and a friend of Wendy, with the consent of Bob. Resign: Bob may end his guardianship of Wendy. End guardian: Those who decide for Wendy, other than Bob, may end Bob's guardianship. Guardian unfriend: Bob may end his friendship with Wendy, which ends his guardianship. Wendy may not end a friendship with her guardian.

3. ■ Ward and person. Ward acquaint: Wendy, a ward of Alice, and Bob may jointly come to know each other. Ward befriend: Wendy may enter a relation with Bob with the consent of Bob and Alice, provided Wendy and Bob know each other and Alice and Bob are friends. Ward end, Unfriend, Ward unfriend: Wendy, Bob or Alice may end the relation of Bob and Wendy.

4. ■ Wards. Wards acquaint: Wendy, a ward of Alice, and Will, a ward of Bob, may jointly come to know each other. Wards befriend: Wendy may enter a relation with Will with the consent of Will, Alice and Bob, provided Wendy and Will know each other, Alice knows Will and is a friend of Bob, Alice and Bob possibly one person.
5. ■ Retire: Those who decide for Wendy may retire Wendy; every guardianship and relation of Wendy then ends and Wendy can take no act.
Organisation
Organisation inherits from Guardians (GSC, From Grassroots Contract to Grassroots App, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06231).

An *organisation* is a ward with *participants*, which include its *officers*, each with a *role*. The *bylaws*, which its founder decides, name the roles of an organisation and say who decides each of its acts and how, their own amendment included.
Alice and Bob are persons, Orga an organisation.
1. ■ Found: Alice, or an organisation with the consent of Alice, may create Orga (Guardians:1); Alice is then its first officer.

2. ■ Acts of the organisation. Propose: An officer, or a person the bylaws name, may propose an act of Orga. Vote: Those who decide the act may vote on it. Act: An officer the bylaws name for the act may take it for Orga after the votes decide it according to the bylaws.

3. ■ Participation. Join: Bob may become a participant of Orga with the consent of those who decide for Orga. Leave, Expel: Either Bob or those who decide for Orga may end Bob's participation, and with it every role he holds.
4. ■ Officers. Appoint: Guardians:2, only if Bob is a participant; the decision names his role.
5. ■ Amend: Those who decide it may amend the bylaws.
6. ○ Accountability. Orga will be accountable at law for its undertakings where it is a juridical person, and every officer who decided an act of Orga will be accountable for it with Orga.
Broadcast
Broadcast inherits from Friendship.
A *broadcast* is a message with a unique identifier, which its maker holds. Δ > 0 is a period of time, and a broadcast is *live* for Δ after it is made.
Alice and Bob are persons.
1. ■ Forward: Alice, who holds a live broadcast, forwards it to her friend Bob, who does not hold it; Bob then holds it.
2. ■ Expire: Alice ceases to hold a broadcast that is not live.
Emergencies
Emergencies inherits from Broadcast and Organisation.

A *personal emergency* is a broadcast that includes the location of its maker, a description and the help its maker asks; it ceases to be live when its maker resolves it. A *village emergency* is a broadcast that includes instructions. A *resolution* of a personal emergency and an *answer* to it are broadcasts.
Alice and Bob are persons, Orga an organisation.
1. ■ Personal emergency: Alice may broadcast a personal emergency, provided she has no live personal emergency of her own.
2. ■ Village emergency: Alice, an officer of Orga, may broadcast a village emergency.
3. ■ Emergency forward: Alice, a participant of Orga, may forward a live village emergency of Orga that she holds to Bob, a participant of Orga, who does not hold it; Bob then holds it.
4. ■ Resolve: Alice may broadcast the resolution of her personal emergency.
5. ■ Answer: Bob, who holds a live personal emergency, may broadcast an answer to it that says the help he will give.
6. ○ Help. Bob will give the help he answered.
Encounters
Encounters inherits from Knowledge (GSC, From Grassroots Contract to Grassroots App, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06231).
A person is *nearby* Alice when her phone reaches theirs by Bluetooth or the local network, without the Internet; a *place* is where Alice is.
Alice and Bob are persons.
1. ■ Open place: Alice may declare the place she is in open. Close place: Alice may close it.
2. ■ Encounter: Alice and Bob, nearby each other, who have both declared the place open, come to know each other.
Groups
Groups inherits from Friendship.
A *message* is what a person sends.
Alice and Bob are persons.
1. ■ Message: Alice may send a message to her friend Bob.
2. ■ Group. Create: Alice may create a group, of which she is the leader and first member. Close: Alice may close the group by leaving it.

3. ■ Joining and Leaving. Join: Alice, the leader of a group, may add her friend Bob to it, with the consent of Bob. Remove, Leave: Either Alice or Bob may then end Bob's membership in the group, which also ends when Alice and Bob cease to be friends.
4. ■ Group messaging. Post: A member of a group may send a message to the group. Deliver: Its leader delivers it to every current member.
Warded Groups
Warded Groups inherits from Groups and Guardians.
Alice is a person, Wendy a ward.
1. ■ A ward's messages. Ward message: Wendy may send a message to a friend (Groups:1). Ward post: Wendy may send a message to a group (Groups:4).
2. ■ A ward's group. Ward create: Wendy may create a group (Groups:2). Ward close: Wendy may close it (Groups:2). Guardian close: Alice, a guardian of Wendy, may close it.
3. ■ Ward join: Wendy may join a group (Groups:3) only with the consent of Alice, a guardian of Wendy.
Children
Children inherits from Warded Groups.
Alice and Bob are persons, Wendy and Will children.
1. ◆ Enter: Guardians:1, only if Alice is a legal parent of the minor who operates Wendy.

2. ■ A child's acquaintances. Child acquaint: Guardians:3, only if Alice knows Bob, and with the consent of Alice. Children acquaint: Guardians:4, only if Alice knows Will and Bob knows Wendy, and with the consent of Alice and Bob, who know each other, Alice and Bob possibly one person.
3. ■ Child create: Warded Groups:2, only with the consent of Alice, a parent of Wendy. Only a child, Will, may join the group, with the consent of Bob, a parent of Will.

4. ○ Of age: The creator of Wendy may declare Wendy of age, which ends every guardianship of Wendy, and Wendy is then a person. The creator will do so if the minor who operates Wendy comes of age, and not before.

5. ○ A minor who is not a ward. Alice, aware that someone is a minor though not a ward, will neither befriend the minor nor let her child befriend the minor, and will report it to the minor's legal parents if she knows who they are.
Notices
Notices inherits from Broadcast and Organisation.
A *notice* is a broadcast that includes its text and the area it is for.
Alice and Bob are persons, Orga an organisation.
1. ■ Notice: Alice, an officer of Orga, may broadcast a notice.
2. ■ Notice forward: Alice, a participant of Orga, may forward a live notice of Orga that she holds to Bob, a participant of Orga, who does not hold it; Bob then holds it.
Overlay
Overlay inherits from Friendship.
Alice, Bob and Carol are persons.
1. ■ Point friend: Alice, who does not point to her friend Bob, may point to Bob.
2. ■ Point transitive: Alice, who knows Carol and points to Bob who points to Carol, may point to Carol.
3. ■ Unpoint: Alice, who points to Bob, may cease pointing to Bob.
Labelled Overlay
Labelled Overlay inherits from Overlay.
A pointer may be labeled by a person, and a pointer labeled by Dave is a *Dave-pointer*. Friends Alice and Bob have a Bob-pointer from Alice to Bob and an Alice-pointer from Bob to Alice.
Alice, Bob, Carol and Dave are persons, Carol and Dave possibly one person.
1. ■ Labeled point friend: Alice, who has no Dave-pointer to her friend Bob, may add one, if Bob has a Dave-pointer.
2. ■ Labeled point transitive: Alice, who knows Carol and either has a Dave-pointer to Bob or is Bob's friend, may add a Dave-pointer to Carol, if Bob has a Dave-pointer to Carol.
3. ■ Labeled unpoint: Alice, who has a Dave-pointer to Carol, may remove it, unless Carol is Dave and her friend.
Feeds
Feeds inherits from Labelled Overlay.
A *feed* is named by its author.
Alice, Bob and Carol are persons, Bob and Carol possibly one person.
1. ■ Post: Alice has a feed and may post to it an item, created or received.
2. ■ Deliver: Alice, who has a Carol-pointer to Bob who knows her, receives from Bob every item of Carol's feed that Bob holds.
3. ■ Labeled point transitive: Labelled Overlay:2, only if Carol knows Alice.
Village Social
Village Social inherits from Friendship, Encounters, Groups, Feeds, Children, Emergencies and Notices.
